gloss: beef (or pork) and egg rice bowl

definitions.gloss: beef (or pork) and egg rice bowl
definitions.explanation: A rice bowl dish topped with sliced beef or pork simmered with onions in a sweet soy-based broth, then bound with beaten egg. Named in contrast to {親子丼|おやこどん}, which uses chicken and egg.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}→昼ご飯：02950_hirugohan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{他人丼|たにんどん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made a beef and egg rice bowl for lunch.

examples.japanese: {他人丼|たにんどん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{親子丼|おやこどん}→親子丼：17621_oyakodon⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{似|に}ている→似る：01159_niru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Tanindon is similar to oyakodon, but the meat is different.

examples.japanese: ⟦{関西|かんさい}→関西：00179_kansai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}→牛肉：02874_gyuuniku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{他人丼|たにんどん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{定番|ていばん}→定番：12265_teiban⟧⟦メニュー→メニュー：11166_menyuu⟧だ。
examples.english: In the Kansai region, beef tanindon is a standard menu item.

notes:
The name is a playful contrast with ⟦{親子丼|おやこどん}→親子丼：17621_oyakodon⟧ (parent-and-child bowl). In ⟦{親子丼|おやこどん}→親子丼：17621_oyakodon⟧, the chicken (⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧, parent) and egg (⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧, child) are related, so they are "parent and child." In {他人丼|たにんどん}, the meat (beef or pork) and egg are from different animals, so they are "⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧" (strangers/unrelated people).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {他人丼|たにんどん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make a tanindon
- ⟦{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}→牛肉：02874_gyuuniku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{他人丼|たにんどん}: beef tanindon
- ⟦{豚肉|ぶたにく}→豚肉：02956_butaniku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{他人丼|たにんどん}: pork tanindon

REGIONAL NOTE:
{他人丼|たにんどん} is more commonly known in the Kansai region. In Kanto, it is sometimes called {開化丼|かいかどん} (civilization bowl), a name dating back to the Meiji era when eating beef became popular.
